conviction_note: No option anchor; abs_move 15 set a little under the name's 18.1% median reaction because the June print bundled the Gilat sale and this one is mainly the quarter plus the first standalone-Allerium picture. p_up 45 rests on the name selling 6 of its last 7 prints and on soft Allerium bookings. The findings sum (-0.7) and the scaled number (-1.5) agree in sign and are both small: nothing found is a sourced, unpriced, company-level number that decides the print.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue consensus about $109m: Benzinga $108.6m (https://it.benzinga.com/quote/CMTL/earnings-forecasts) and Earnings Whispers $109.3m (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CMTL). The two sources roughly agree on revenue but disagree on EPS (-$0.28 vs -$0.35). The company gives no guidance (Q3 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000023197/000002319726000070/fy26q3ex991earningsrelease.htm). If S&S moves to discontinued operations, a consolidated consensus is not like-for-like, so the bar is effectively disputed and every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is 1.43% of float and about 1 day to cover (FINRA 2026-06-30 settlement via Benzinga, https://it.benzinga.com/quote/CMTL/short-interest; curvedtrading shows the same, updated 2026-07-14, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmtl/). No later settlement was retrievable because the Nasdaq API returned 503. This is not a crowded short. There is no usable skew: the chain is not two-sided. The put/call open-interest ratio is 0.3 on 1,103 contracts, per the baseline. The stock is -14.8% over 20 days, 78.8% off its high and 7.6% above its 52-week low.

findings.finding: The 8-K of 2026-08-03 shows lenders waived the excess-cash-flow prepayment for FY ended 2026-07-31. The company prepaid $10m of term loans from the Gilat advance on 2026-07-31, on top of $1m of scheduled amortisation. The revolver was repaid in May and is undrawn. Liquidity therefore improved into fiscal year-end, and the 10-K is unlikely to revive going-concern language.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June print bundled the sale with capital-structure relief (covenant tests suspended to July 2027) and fell 42.9%, so relief on this line has not been paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K is public, and the stock fell from about $1.68 (end of July) to $1.27 after it. That suggests the market reads the common as a stub behind $220m of preferred and about $220m of debt, so it has ignored deleveraging. If this were priced as relief, the stock would have held its August level.
findings.independence: The Q3 release shows a fifth straight quarter of positive operating cash flow and covenant testing suspended through 2027-07-31 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000023197/000002319726000070/fy26q3ex991earningsrelease.htm). That is the same company's disclosure, a different document.

findings.finding: Gilat's definitive agreement was signed 2026-06-14, before the 2026-07-31 fiscal year-end. Q4 should therefore present the S&S business being sold as held for sale and likely as discontinued operations. The 10-Q states held-for-sale criteria were not met only at April 30. Reported continuing-operations revenue could then land near Allerium plus retained cyber (about $55-75m) against aggregator consensus near $109m. Any carrying-value excess over the $157.5m price would book as a loss on the disposal group.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print with discontinued operations. Reported-quarter misses were sold: Q3 revenue of $106.0m vs about $110.2m estimate fell 42.9% (bundled with the sale), and Q2 fell 24.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregator consensus still carries a consolidated $108.6-109.3m. If the presentation change were in the bar, consensus would sit near the Allerium-plus-cyber run rate. This is an inference from the accounting standard, not something the company confirmed. On a thin, retail-held name the headline optics can move it.
findings.independence: The Gilat 6-K for the period ended 2026-06-30 shows a $10m advance recorded and closing expected by end of 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000897322/000117891326003967/exhibit_99-1.htm). This confirms the agreement predates fiscal year-end, but it is not the presentation itself.

findings.finding: Allerium is the business that remains. It printed a 0.32x book-to-bill in Q3 (vs 0.91x a year earlier). No Allerium contract-win release has followed the 2026-03-25 Oklahoma award, the 2026-04-08 Kentucky milestone and the May Gatineau facility. Q4 bookings and the forward picture for the standalone company are therefore likely soft.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Allerium 'reset' was the focus of the Q3 call, a print that fell 42.9%. Before that, the Q2 print fell 24.5% despite a $107m Tier-1 carrier extension.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced: the 0.32x figure is public, and the stock fell 15% in 20 days into the print. The absence of new award releases through 2026-10-14 is a proxy, not a company number. Had the market fully priced a further Allerium decline, the stock would sit at or below its 52-week low rather than 7.6% above it.
findings.independence: The company's own press-release record shows no Allerium award after March 2026 (https://comtech.com/press-releases/2026/03/25/911-association-of-central-oklahoma-governments-selects-allerium-to-deliver-next-generation-9-1-1-call-routing-network/). This is an absence-based proxy that shares the company as its source. Net of the rest: the retained cyber business is about $20m revenue and $3m EBITDA per the Q3 call coverage, too small to offset.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-01 the board added Christopher Maloney, founder and former CEO of TriTech (public-safety software, sold to Bain) and later CEO of SOMA Global, as a seventh director. The CEO framed it as building Allerium's position after the S&S sale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on a board change. The June 16 5.02 8-K coincided with the -42.9% print and cannot be separated from it.
findings.why_not_priced: Announced 2026-10-05, and the stock has drifted since. It matters only if the call frames a public-safety strategy, or a later Allerium sale, that the appointment foreshadows. It is mostly colour.

outside_window.finding: Gilat closing of the $157.5m S&S purchase (net about $143-145m; 65% to senior debt) is expected 'toward year-end' or 'by end of 2026', subject to CFIUS and HSR. No clearance has been reported as of 2026-10-14, and closing will not happen inside the window. The release may update timing, which is folded into abs_move.
Lender warrants for 625,000 shares at $0.10 vest on 2026-10-17 unless the related loans are repaid first (about 2% dilution). This lands after the 2026-10-15 close.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. A small negative lean agrees with the -14.8% 20-day run-up and the name's history of selling prints (1 up in 7), so it is probably partly priced, which is why p_up sits at 45 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (verify the bar): the revenue bar has two roughly agreeing sources, but the discontinued-operations basis makes it effectively disputed. The accounting-optics finding was cut from -0.8 to -0.6 and every finding kept small.
Rule 5 (a narrow proxy and an absence are small): the Allerium bookings finding rests partly on the absence of award releases, so it was cut from -0.8 to -0.6.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the money buys deleveraging, a waived excess-cash-flow sweep and an undrawn revolver, so the financing finding stays positive at +0.4.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest is 1.43% with about 1 day to cover. Not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk.
The board appointment was cut from +0.2 to +0.1: it is not a company number and has no in-window mechanism.
abs_move_pct, p_up and print_vs_bar_pct are unchanged.
